name: JIT & HotSpot Tiered Compilation
tagline: Profiling running bytecode to identify hot loops and call sites, then speculatively compiling them to native machine code with fast deoptimization traps.
purpose: Build a progressive mental model of JIT compilation—from C1/C2 tiered compilation and megamorphic inline caches to escape analysis scalar replacement and AppCDS/CRaC warmup.

spark.summary: Tiered JIT compilers profile running bytecode to identify hot loops and call sites, then speculatively compile them into native machine code with fast deoptimization guards.
spark.keyTakeaway: Speculate with a safety net: the JIT makes dynamic, polymorphic code as fast as static C++ by assuming the common case and trapping back to the interpreter if assumptions break.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Pure interpreters pay a 10x–50x dispatch tax per instruction, while static AOT compilers cannot inline virtual calls across dynamically loaded plugins.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Tiered JIT Compilation & Speculative Deoptimization State Machine (INTERPRETER (T0) -> C1 TIERS (T1-T3) -> C2 PEAK (T4)); Synthetic Warmup Before Readiness Probe Admission (New JVM Pod -> C1 / C2 Compiler -> K8s Readiness).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Choose the compilation model based on startup SLA vs. peak throughput. Sending 100% live traffic to a brand-new cold JVM pod during an HPA scale-out triggers **deoptimization and JIT CPU spikes** right when latency is already stressed.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore escape analysis, serverless cold-start mitigation, and JVM garbage collection internals.

learningJourney.title: What is Tiered JIT Compilation
learningJourney.explanation:
Pure interpreters pay a 10x–50x dispatch tax per instruction, while static AOT compilers cannot inline virtual calls across dynamically loaded plugins. **Tiered JIT compilation** (HotSpot C1→C2, V8 Ignition→Sparkplug→TurboFan, .NET RyuJIT) combines both.

Bytecode starts interpreted (`Tier 0`), moves to fast-compiling **C1** (`Tiers 1–3`) to collect branch and type profiles (MDOs), and hot methods (`>10,000` invocations) graduate to **C2** (`Tier 4`) for speculative inlining, SIMD vectorization, and escape analysis.

learningJourney.title: Why Speculative Inlining & Escape Analysis Unlock C++-Speed Code
learningJourney.explanation: Using Class Hierarchy Analysis (CHA) and runtime type profiles, C2 devirtualizes and inlines interface calls like `List.get()` when 99% of calls hit `ArrayList`. Once inlined, **Escape Analysis** (`-XX:+DoEscapeAnalysis`) proves whether a `new Point(x, y)` escapes the method—eliminating the heap allocation completely via **scalar replacement** into CPU registers.

ideas.title: Monomorphic vs. Megamorphic Inline Caches
ideas.description: Call sites seeing 1 concrete class (monomorphic) inline directly; >2–4 classes (megamorphic) fall back to virtual table dispatch, causing 3x–10x slowdowns in V8/JVM.

ideas.title: 325-Bytecode Inlining Ceiling
ideas.description: HotSpot refuses to inline hot methods larger than `-XX:FreqInlineSize=325` bytecodes—keep hot helpers small and cohesive.

learningJourney.title: Where JIT Shines (and Where AOT Native Binaries Win)
learningJourney.explanation: JIT compilation trades initial warmup CPU and code-cache RAM for peak steady-state throughput.

comparison.choice: Good Candidate: Long-Running Backend Services (JVM / .NET / V8)
benefits: Seconds of warmup pay off over hours/days of peak profile-guided optimization.
costs: Cold instances suffer 5x–10x higher latency during the first 30–120 seconds unless warmed up.

comparison.choice: Avoid: Short-Lived CLIs & Serverless Lambdas (<500 ms)
benefits: GraalVM Native Image, Go, or Rust AOT binaries start in `<15 ms` with zero JIT warmup.
costs: JIT compilation overhead exceeds total function execution time.

comparison.choice: Avoid: Tightly Constrained Embedded (<64 MB RAM)
benefits: AOT binaries need no 240 MB JIT `CodeCache` or profiling MDOs.
costs: JIT metadata and code cache blow small memory budgets.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: Code Cache Sizing, Escape Analysis & Warmup Mitigation
learningJourney.explanation: Monitor `CodeCache` usage via JMX/Prometheus (`-XX:+UseCodeCacheFlushing` if needed), and mitigate autoscaling cold-start cascades with **AppCDS** (`-XX:ArchiveClassesAtExit`), **CRaC** checkpoints, or synthetic warmup traffic before readiness probes pass.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```bash
# Inspect JIT compilation, inlining decisions, and code cache sizing
java \
  -XX:+UnlockDiagnosticVMOptions \
  -XX:+PrintCompilation \
  -XX:ReservedCodeCacheSize=256m \
  -XX:+UseCodeCacheFlushing \
  -XX:SharedArchiveFile=app-cds.jsa \
  -jar service.jar
```

knowledgeCheck.question: How does HotSpot C2's Escape Analysis (`-XX:+DoEscapeAnalysis`) reduce GC pressure on hot loops?

options.text: When C2 proves a newly allocated object never escapes the method or thread, scalar replacement decomposes its fields directly into CPU registers or stack slots, skipping heap allocation
options.feedback: Correct: zero heap allocation means zero Eden churn and zero GC work.

options.text: It moves all objects from Eden directly into Old Generation
options.feedback: Promoting to Old Gen would increase Major GC pressure rather than eliminating allocation.

options.text: It disables garbage collection during loops
options.feedback: GC safepoints still exist; escape analysis simply avoids allocating non-escaping objects.
